The States parties declare that they recognize the principles of Part II as human rights and fundamental freedoms founded on the general principles of law recognized by civilized nations: no final counterpart; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Every State must ensure: (a) laws securing the rights to all within its jurisdiction, whether citizens, aliens or stateless; (b) conformity of those laws with general principles of law; (c) an effective remedy even against acts of officials; (d) enforcement by an independent judiciary; (e) police and executive officers who support the rights; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

When the Secretary-General asks under a General Assembly resolution, a party's Government must explain how its law gives effect to any provision of the Bill; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Life: unlawful to deprive anyone of life except in executing a court sentence on conviction for a crime carrying that penalty. Para. 2 makes abortion unlawful except where the law permits it, done in good faith, to save the woman's life, on medical advice (hereditary mental disease) or after rape; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Unlawful to subject anyone against his will to physical mutilation or to medical or scientific experimentation; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Unlawful to subject anyone to torture in any form or to cruel or inhuman indignity; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

No slavery or servitude; no forced or compulsory labour except as punishment after conviction. Forced labour excludes military service (or alternative service for conscientious objectors), service in emergencies or calamities, and minor communal services; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

No arbitrary arrest or detention. Deprivation of liberty is allowed only in listed cases (a)-(g). There is a right to be told the charges promptly, to be brought promptly before a judge and to trial within a reasonable time or release, a habeas corpus remedy, and an enforceable right to compensation for unlawful arrest; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

No imprisonment or holding in servitude merely for breach of a contractual obligation; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Anyone not under lawful deprivation of liberty or outstanding national-service obligations is free to leave any country, including his own; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

No alien legally admitted to a State's territory may be arbitrarily expelled; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

A fair hearing before an independent and impartial tribunal on criminal charges or civil rights and obligations, with a qualified representative of one's choice. No conviction or punishment except after public trial; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

No guilt for an act that was not an offence when committed, and no heavier punishment than the law then prescribed; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

No one may be deprived of juridical personality. Civil rights may be restricted only for minors, persons of unsound mind and persons convicted of crimes that carry such restriction by law; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Freedom of religion, conscience and belief: to hold, manifest and change belief and to worship. Freedom to give and receive religious teaching and to persuade other adults; parents or guardians decide a minor's teaching. Limitations only as prescribed by law and necessary for public order and welfare, morals and the rights and freedoms of others; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Freedom of expression and information, in two alternative texts. The Drafting Committee draft: express and publish ideas, receive and disseminate information, with listed restrictions. The United States draft: freedom of information, speech and expression, including holding opinions and seeking, receiving and imparting information; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Right to assemble peaceably for any lawful purpose. Restrictions only for protection of life or property, prevention of disorders, or preventing obstruction of traffic or the free movement of others; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Freedom to form associations, in any form lawful under State law, for legitimate interests and any lawful object. Associations enjoy the rights in arts. 15 and 16; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Everyone is entitled to the Bill's rights without distinction as to race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, property status, or national or social origin. Everyone is entitled to equal protection under the law; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

No article text. The heading '(Article 20)' is in parentheses and is followed only by a United States observer's suggestion to replace the specific limitations in each article with one general limitation clause: no final counterpart; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Open for accession to UN Members, parties to the ICJ Statute and States the General Assembly declares eligible. Accession is by deposit with the Secretary-General. Entry into force once two-thirds of UN Members have deposited, and on deposit for later accessions. Each deposit carries a statement of constitutional approval and a declaration that national law gives full effect to Part II. The Secretary-General notifies States; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Federal clause. For articles fit for federal action, the federal government has the same obligations as a unitary State. For articles within the competence of constituent states, provinces or cantons, it only refers them to those authorities with a favourable recommendation; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Colonial clause: the Bill applies to a party's colonies, overseas, protected, mandated or trust territories when the State accedes on their behalf. The State is to seek those governments' consent promptly: no final counterpart; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

Amendments enter into force when adopted by two-thirds of the General Assembly and ratified by two-thirds of the parties. They bind only the parties that ratify them; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)

The articles of the Bill form an inseparable and organic whole: no final counterpart; the Geneva working group's draft Convention (E/CN.4/56, December 1947), debated with the Declaration in the Commission's plenary (E/CN.4/SR.34-42); read by hand (two independent readings reconciled)
